fact: The Algerian Space Agency (ASAL) says it works with the Ministry of Agriculture on pilot satellite mapping of cereals (Sidi Bel Abbes, Sentinel-2 NDVI time series) and of potatoes (Mostaganem), and plans to customise CropWatch for these two pilot zones.

The CGIAR tool series says the WaPOR-based Water Use Tool is used by the WaPOR Digital Unit at the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development, hosted by its Department of Statistics and Strategies, and uses 20 m WaPOR satellite data to compute dekadal irrigation water use and map irrigated and rainfed parcels, with a dashboard for the Mitidja West scheme.
Algeria's agriculture minister announced that from December 2022 a census of irrigated cereal perimeters would use satellite images, plus 100 drones in some wilayas.

fact: Algeria's agriculture minister and the space agency ASAL held a study day on 21 June 2020 to set a roadmap for using satellite images and maps to define farmland perimeters in the Saharan south, ASAL saying its imagery delimits cultivable land and groundwater.

Les Enjeux Eco reports the agriculture ministry's secretary general saying satellite imagery from the Algerian Space Agency let Algeria control the locust invasion, with 23,000 hectares treated preventively and eight field teams deployed in the south.

ASAL states that its first national conference on geospatial technologies for agriculture, held 29-30 November 2023 in Oran, heard presentations on ASAL's agriculture studies, Alsat-1B imagery to identify desert soils for farming, and the CropWatch crop-monitoring experience in Algeria.
